scope: Two local synthetic Node.js probes of one possible descriptor-path technique; not a Bug47 exploit reproduction or remedy

probes.question: Can a held directory descriptor be traversed through /dev/fd/<fd>/item before or after replacing its original pathname?
probes.setup: Owned /private/tmp tree with trusted/item and outside/item; open trusted with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, then rename trusted and replace that pathname with a link to outside.

probes.question: Is /dev/fd/<fd> itself a usable directory path for normal Node filesystem traversal?
probes.setup: Owned /private/tmp directory with item; keep its O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW descriptor open in the same process.

fixture_custody: Both uniquely created /private/tmp/mdkg-bug47-fd-probe-* trees were removed in finally blocks. A subsequent max-depth-one directory check found no matching roots.
interpretation: On this macOS/Node combination, substituting /dev/fd/<directory-fd>/child for openat is not a usable traversal primitive. This does not establish that every Node-only design is impossible, nor does it prove Linux behavior or Bug47 exploitability.
not_performed: No source patch, candidate package build, Git action or provider action.
No Linux executor, native addon, system-tool bridge, hosted CI or blocked security context.
No synchronized outside-root attack or full Bug47 remediation test.
release_effect: Bug47 remains an unresolved 0.6.0 publication blocker. Dec97's deferral is not a waiver.
